target.title: fix(daemon): refuse duplicate launchd gateway managers
target.body:
Closes #97178

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running the gateway under a system-domain LaunchDaemon could later run `openclaw gateway install` from a user session and silently add a duplicate gui-domain LaunchAgent for the same gateway label and port. That duplicate manager setup can restart-loop the gateway and disconnect clients.

## Why This Change Was Made

The macOS launchd installer now checks for a same-label system LaunchDaemon before it writes or bootstraps the user LaunchAgent. If `launchctl print system/<label>` succeeds or a matching `/Library/LaunchDaemons/<label>.plist` exists, install refuses with recovery guidance instead of creating a second KeepAlive manager. This intentionally stays narrow and does not add full system LaunchDaemon install/stop/uninstall lifecycle support.

AI-assisted: yes. I understand the change: it adds a pre-write launchd conflict guard and focused mocked launchd regressions for the reported duplicate-manager path.

## User Impact

Headless macOS operators who already manage the gateway as a system LaunchDaemon get a clear stop-and-fix error instead of a second user LaunchAgent that can fight the system daemon on the same port.

## Evidence

Behavior addressed: `openclaw gateway install` refuses to write/bootstrap a gui-domain LaunchAgent when a same-label system LaunchDaemon is loaded or present on disk.

Real environment tested: local source checkout with mocked launchd states; the issue reporter supplied live headless macOS LaunchDaemon evidence on #97178. I did not mutate a real system LaunchDaemon on this host.

Exact steps:

```shell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/daemon/launchd.test.ts src/daemon/inspect.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/status.gather.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Evidence after fix: the new launchd tests cover both `launchctl print system/ai.openclaw.gateway` reporting a loaded daemon and `/Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` existing when the system job is not printed.

Observed result: focused launchd test passed; the broader daemon/status proof set passed in 2 Vitest shards.

What was not tested: live install against a disposable headless macOS host with a real system LaunchDaemon, to avoid creating or disturbing host-level launchd services from this automation run.


---

**Runtime proof — captured before/after (negative-control harness, macOS, Node 22):**

Exercised end-to-end through the real `installLaunchAgent` → `writeLaunchAgentPlist` → `assertNoSystemLaunchDaemonConflict` → real `execFile` path; only the external `launchctl` binary is mocked (a PATH shim), plist writes go to a scratch `HOME`. Same harness ran on unfixed `main` and on this branch.

_Before — unfixed `main` (negative control):_

```
Scenario A (no conflict, proceeds)  : PASS
Scenario B (conflict, refuses)      : FAIL
>>> UNFIXED: with a same-label system LaunchDaemon present, install did NOT
    refuse and WROTE the gui LaunchAgent plist anyway.  (the #97178 bug)
```

_After — this branch:_

```
Scenario A (no conflict, proceeds)  : PASS
Scenario B (conflict, refuses)      : PASS
error (verbatim): Existing system LaunchDaemon system/ai.openclaw.gateway detected at
  /Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist. Refusing to install a gui-domain
  LaunchAgent for the same gateway label because duplicate launchd managers can
  restart-loop the gateway. ... sudo launchctl bootout system/ai.openclaw.gateway ...
plist written : false
>>> FIXED: the guard refused the duplicate manager with recovery guidance.
```

**What was not tested:** a live install against a disposable macOS host with a real system LaunchDaemon over a live port; and the on-disk `/Library/LaunchDaemons/<label>.plist` branch (needs a root-owned path via `sudo touch`/`rm`) — it shares the same throw site as the proven `launchctl print` branch.


---

**Branch-(b) proof — REAL root-owned `/Library/LaunchDaemons` plist (addresses the "mock-backed proof" review note):**

Re-ran on macOS with a genuine root-owned `/Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` (`sudo touch`), and with `launchctl print system/<label>` forced to report NOT-loaded (exit 113) so the **only** conflict signal is the real on-disk system plist — the `launchctl` shim plays no part in the decision. This exercises the real `/Library/LaunchDaemons` filesystem check (`LAUNCH_DAEMON_SYSTEM_DIR`) end-to-end.

_PR branch (`9f0f82df78`) — exit 0:_

```
launchctl print system/<label> : NOT-loaded (113)  -> branch-(a) inert
real /Library/LaunchDaemons plist present : yes     -> branch-(b) is the signal
install threw  : true
error (verbatim):
  | Existing system LaunchDaemon system/ai.openclaw.gateway detected at /Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist.
  | Refusing to install a gui-domain LaunchAgent for the same gateway label because duplicate launchd managers can restart-loop the gateway.
  | Keep the system LaunchDaemon, or remove it first with `sudo launchctl bootout system/ai.openclaw.gateway` and `sudo rm /Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist`, then rerun `openclaw gateway install`.
gui LaunchAgent written : false
>>> FIXED: install refused via the REAL root-owned system plist (branch-b).
```

_`main` (`29f5e9d35c`, no guard) — exit 1, negative control:_

```
launchctl print system/<label> : NOT-loaded (113)   real plist present : yes
install threw  : false
gui LaunchAgent written : true
>>> UNFIXED: install IGNORED the real system plist and wrote the gui LaunchAgent anyway — the #97178 bug.
```

target.title: refactor(infra): consolidate bounded HTTP body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bounded HTTP response reads were owned by the private media package even though the primitive is transport infrastructure used across agents, gateway, plugins, media, and provider flows. That left HTTP lifecycle behavior coupled to a media-domain package and duplicated its ownership alongside request-body handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Moves the existing exact Web `Response` byte-limit implementation into `src/infra/http-body.ts`, preserving overflow, idle-timeout, cancellation, reader-lock, fallback, decoding, and caller-provided error behavior. Core callers and the existing Plugin SDK facades now use the infra owner; JSON/text interpretation, status handling, retries, logging, and provider policy remain with callers. The private `@openclaw/media-core/read-response-with-limit` subpath and its build/alias scaffolding are removed.

The deprecated `plugin-sdk/infra-runtime` barrel is pinned to its pre-existing request-body exports so the relocated response readers remain available only through the focused `response-limit-runtime` and existing `media-runtime` surfaces.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Maintainers and plugin authors keep the same supported Plugin SDK response-limit APIs, with one canonical core owner for bounded HTTP request and response reads.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `b5ed973ce800463d49e27067c620682f4c7f6657`.

target.title: fix(embedded-agent): strip stale thinking signatures on replay_invalid retry
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Thinking blocks from a prior provider context carry valid cryptographic signatures that survive replay sanitization, causing permanent `replay_invalid` rejection after process restart with thinking policy changed. Strip thinking signatures on retry after `replay_invalid` detection.

- **Problem**: When a session accumulates thinking blocks under `thinkingDefault: adaptive` and the gateway restarts with `thinkingDefault: off`, `sanitizeSessionHistory` runs `stripStaleThinkingSignaturesForCompactionReplay` (compaction-only, no-op without compaction) and `stripInvalidThinkingSignatures` (only strips blank/empty signatures). The valid-but-now-stale signatures reach Anthropic → `replay_invalid` 400. The embedded runner retries 3+ times with the same unstripped messages → all fail identically → `"Use /new to start a fresh session."`
- **Solution**: Add `stripAllThinkingSignatures` that unconditionally strips thinking signatures from all assistant messages. Pass `replayInvalid` flag through the attempt params chain. When `replayInvalid` is true, call `stripAllThinkingSignatures` before the existing compaction-specific stripping chain. One-shot gate prevents infinite loop.
- **What changed**: `thinking.ts` (new `stripAllThinkingSignatures`), `replay-history.ts` (conditional strip in `sanitizeSessionHistory`), `run/types.ts` (param), `run.ts` (pass state), `attempt.ts` (pass to sanitize)
- **What did NOT change**: Normal replay path, compaction-stripping, `dropThinkingBlocks`, `preserveLatestAssistant`, auth rotation

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #99654
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The existing thinking-signature stripping pipeline has two tools: `stripStaleThinkingSignaturesForCompactionReplay` (compaction-timestamp-based, #90163) and `stripInvalidThinkingSignatures` (absent/blank signatures). Neither handles the non-compaction restart case where thinking blocks carry valid cryptographic signatures from a prior provider context — on process restart with `thinkingDefault: off` those signatures become stale and Anthropic rejects every replay attempt. Each failed retry costs a paid API call, and the session is permanently lost.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: replay_invalid thinking-signature rejection on process restart with thinking policy change
- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22.19, `fix/replay-invalid-thinking-strip-99654` branch
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { stripAllThinkingSignatures, stripStaleThinkingSignaturesForCompactionReplay } from './src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/thinking.ts';

// Messages with thinking blocks carrying valid signatures
const msgs = [
  { role: "user", content: "hello" },
  { role: "assistant", content: [
    { type: "thinking", thinking: "Let me analyze...", signature: "sig_abc123" },
    { type: "text", text: "My answer" }
  ]},
  { role: "user", content: "follow up" },
  { role: "assistant", content: [
    { type: "thinking", thinking: "More thinking...", thinkingSignature: "sig_def456" },
    { type: "tool_use", name: "exec" }
  ]},
];

// Test 1: strip all signatures
const beforeCount = (JSON.stringify(msgs).match(/signature|thinkingSignature/g) || []).length;
const out1 = stripAllThinkingSignatures(msgs);
const afterCount1 = (JSON.stringify(out1).match(/signature|thinkingSignature/g) || []).length;
console.log("Test 1:", beforeCount, "->", afterCount1, "Stripped?", beforeCount > 0 && afterCount1 === 0);
NODE
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
... [production function call] ...

=== Test 1: stripAllThinkingSignatures ===
Before: 2 After: 0 Stripped: YES

=== Test 2: preserveLatestAssistant=true ===
Last sig preserved: YES

=== Test 3: Non-thinking content preserved ===
Tool_use preserved: PASS
Text preserved: PASS
User msg unchanged: PASS

=== Test 4: Compaction-only strip (no compaction, no-op) ===
Signatures preserved: PASS (expected)

=== Test 5: No thinking blocks (no-op) ===
Reference equal: PASS
```

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. `stripAllThinkingSignatures` strips all `signature`/`thinkingSignature` fields from assistant messages (2→0 in test)
  2. `preserveLatestAssistant=true` correctly preserves the last assistant's thinking signature
  3. Non-thinking content (tool_use, text blocks, user messages) is completely untouched
  4. `stripStaleThinkingSignaturesForCompactionReplay` remains a correct no-op without compaction
  5. When no thinking blocks exist, reference equality is preserved (zero overhead)
  6. Unit tests: 3 test files, 123 tests passed
- **What was not tested**: Live Anthropic API round-trip (requires API key with thinking-enabled access). The fix relies on source-level verification against the reported `"Invalid signature in thinking block"` error pattern and the proven `stripThinkingSignaturesFromMessage` infrastructure.

## Root Cause

The `sanitizeSessionHistory` pipeline at `replay-history.ts:744-756` only handles compaction-stale signatures (via `stripStaleThinkingSignaturesForCompactionReplay`) and absent/blank signatures (via `stripInvalidThinkingSignatures`). Valid cryptographic signatures from a prior provider context survive both filters and trigger Anthropic `replay_invalid` on every retry.

Provenance:
- `stripStaleThinkingSignaturesForCompactionReplay`: introduced by #90163 (Jun 4, 2026) — compaction-only scope
- `stripInvalidThinkingSignatures`: existed before — only handles absent/blank signatures
- Made visible by: user restarting gateway with `thinkingDefault: off` after accumulating thinking blocks
- Confidence: **clear**

## Regression Test Plan

- `thinking.test.ts` (49 tests): covers `stripThinkingSignaturesFromMessage`, `stripInvalidThinkingSignatures`, `stripStaleThinkingSignaturesForCompactionReplay`
- `replay-history.test.ts` (28 tests): covers `sanitizeSessionHistory`
- `sanitize-session-history.test.ts` (71 tests): covers policy interactions
- Combined: 123 tests pass after change

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Sessions affected by `replay_invalid` thinking-signature errors after process restart will automatically recover (strip signatures + retry once) instead of showing "Use /new to start a fresh session." Users with no `replay_invalid` experience no behavioral change.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Minimal (1 new function + 1 conditional call in the existing pipeline), reactive (only fires on `replayInvalid`), uses proven `stripThinkingSignaturesFromMessage` helper.
- **Refactor needed**: No.
- **Alternative considered**: Preventative approach (strip all thinking signatures when `thinkingDefault: off`). Rejected because it changes normal replay semantics; reactive approach is safer.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Latest assistant thinking block**: `preserveLatestAssistant` option available (default `false`; safe in replay path where a new user turn is appended after the latest assistant)
- **Over-stripping**: `replayInvalid` gate ensures strip only fires on retry after `replay_invalid` detection
- **Infinite loop**: `accumulatedReplayState.replayInvalid` set once; run-iteration limit bounds total attempts
- **Compatibility**: Independent of open PR #94649 (different recovery path)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

Related to #99654

target.title: fix: keep OpenClaw control tools available when tool_search misroutes
target.body:
Closes #99464
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server workers could be told to discover OpenClaw session/control tools through `tool_search`, but `tool_search` could resolve a different connector universe and leave the worker without the OpenClaw delegation controls it needed.

It also avoids changing the registered `heartbeat_respond` schema between normal and heartbeat turns on a resumed Codex thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the small, stable OpenClaw control set (`agents_list`, `sessions_spawn`, and `sessions_yield`) directly available on every Codex app-server turn. Broad tools remain deferred behind `tool_search`, and `heartbeat_respond` remains deferred with stable registration across normal and heartbeat turns.

This keeps delegation controls reliable without making the entire OpenClaw tool catalog direct, and preserves the Codex app-server requirement that a resumed thread retain the same registered dynamic-tool definitions.

## User Impact

Codex app-server agents can reliably list agents, spawn subagents, and yield without depending on connector-oriented `tool_search` resolution. Existing deferred-tool behavior remains in place for the broader catalog, and heartbeat turns no longer risk a thread schema mismatch.

## Evidence

- Live AWS Crabbox before/after proof: run `run_0a496ddc9d30`, provider `aws`, lease `cbx_60d63e7d43b5` (`harbor-prawn`).

target.title: fix: keep text tool results ahead of stale media placeholders
target.body:
Closes #99241

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users reading text-only tool output could see or receive model responses based on media-placeholder text such as `(see attached image)` when a replayed or transformed tool result carried stale image/media blocks alongside the real text.

The affected workflow is agent/provider-bound handling of tool results during transcript replay, compaction, and provider message conversion. The visible symptom is that a plain text tool result can be misrepresented to the model as an image placeholder.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit text in a `toolResult` now wins over stale media blocks across provider transforms. Media placeholder fallback is reserved for media-only tool results, while mixed text/media tool results preserve the text and suppress stale image/audio placeholders.

This PR is intentionally limited to the minimal functional fix and regression coverage. It does not include the optional default-off diagnostic tracing used during local investigation.

AI-assisted: prepared with OpenClaw subagents and reviewed manually before submission.

## User Impact

Users can expect plain text tool results to remain visible to the model as text, even if replay or provider conversion encounters stale media blocks from adjacent tool output. Media-only tool results continue to use the existing placeholder behavior for providers that cannot consume the original media.

Operators get a narrower, provider-level fix without a Control UI change, config change, migration, or new runtime option.

## Evidence

- Focused regression tests via the repository wrapper:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts src/llm/providers/tool-result-text.test.ts src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts src/llm/providers/google-shared.convert.test.ts extensions/google/transport-stream.test.ts src/llm/providers/mistral.test.ts src/llm/providers/openai-completions.test.ts`

target.title: fix(telegram): harden rich send fallback and typing breaker
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes the remaining Telegram runtime behaviors from #99471:

- Raise the default typing-start breaker from 2 to 5 consecutive failures so transient `sendChatAction` failures do not silence typing feedback too aggressively.
- Treat `RICH_MESSAGE_CONTENT_REQUIRED` like the existing Telegram rich-message validation failures and fall back to plain text when there is sendable fallback text.
- Guard empty rendered rich-message payloads before `sendRichMessage`, and let chunked durable delivery skip unsendable empty rich chunks instead of aborting later valid chunks.

The rich-message reply-context text extraction portion of #99471 is already present on current `main`; this branch is based on current `main` and leaves that existing fix intact.

Closes #99471

## Implementation notes

- `src/channels/typing.ts` now uses a named default of 5 consecutive failures while preserving explicit overrides and existing success-reset behavior.
- `extensions/telegram/src/send-error-predicates.ts` now shares a rich-message plain-text fallback predicate for invalid rich entities and `RICH_MESSAGE_CONTENT_REQUIRED`.
- Both Telegram send funnels are kept aligned:
  - `extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.ts`
  - `extensions/telegram/src/send.ts`
- Regression tests cover:
  - default typing breaker trips after five failures, not two;
  - durable rich send falls back on `RICH_MESSAGE_CONTENT_REQUIRED`;
  - delivery rich send falls back on `RICH_MESSAGE_CONTENT_REQUIRED`;
  - empty rich text is rejected before calling Telegram's raw `sendRichMessage`.

## Validation

Local lightweight prechecks:

- `corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/channels/typing.ts src/channels/typing.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/send-error-predicates.ts extensions/telegram/src/send.ts extensions/telegram/src/send.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.test.ts` — passed
- `git diff --check -- src/channels/typing.ts src/channels/typing.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/send-error-predicates.ts extensions/telegram/src/send.ts extensions/telegram/src/send.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.test.ts` — passed

CI is expected to provide the full targeted test/build signal for this PR.

## Risk

Low to moderate:

- Typing feedback may continue retrying longer during transient channel typing failures, but still stops after a bounded number of consecutive failures.
- Rich-message fallback only catches Telegram validation/content-required errors; other send failures still propagate.
- Empty rich chunks without sendable plain text are skipped in the durable chunk loop to preserve later valid chunks.

target.title: Add Teams delegated auth for plugin tools
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Plugin tools could not safely request a per-user Microsoft Teams delegated token from the current Teams conversation.
- Why it matters: Teams/Graph OBO-style integrations need user-delegated context without leaking channel tokens into prompts, transcripts, or broad plugin surfaces.
- What changed: Added generic plugin delegated-auth policy, runtime propagation, Teams Bot Framework SSO handling, Codex tool forwarding, docs, and a production-shaped example plugin/downstream API.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Delegated auth is implemented for Microsoft Teams only; non-Teams channels are not broadened by this PR.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes N/A
- Related N/A
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: End-to-end Teams delegated-auth consent for an OpenClaw plugin tool, including missing-consent handling, Bot Framework sign-in fallback, six-digit code completion, and retrying the tool with delegated auth available.
- Real environment tested: Local macOS OpenClaw dev checkout, `pnpm openclaw --dev gateway`, Microsoft Teams dev app, Bot Framework OAuth connection, devtunnel on port 3978, local downstream OBO API, and the example `msteams-graph-profile` plugin.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Started the local downstream OBO API.
  2. Started the OpenClaw dev gateway with the Teams channel and `msteams-graph-profile` plugin configured.
  3. Sent `hi, run teams whoami` to the OpenClaw Teams dev app.
  4. Opened the Bot Framework sign-in link rendered in Teams.
  5. Completed Microsoft sign-in/consent and sent the six-digit fallback code back to the Teams chat.
  6. Sent `hi, run teams whoami` again.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): Teams chat screenshot plus copied live output:
  ![Teams delegated auth proof](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/MSNexploder/b74c1786560f164ff726f52605204e33/raw/teams-delegated-auth-proof.png)
  ```text
  msteams_whoami ran again. Result:
  Microsoft Teams delegated auth unavailable: missing_consent

  Microsoft Teams delegated auth is connected. Retry the tool now.

  Success again:
  Stefan Stüben <redacted email>
  ```
- Observed result after fix: The initial tool run requested consent, the six-digit fallback completed the Teams delegated-auth flow, and the retried `msteams_whoami` call returned the signed-in Teams user profile/email through the downstream OBO API.
- What was not tested: Non-Teams channels, production-hosted downstream API deployment, broad tenant rollout beyond the dev tenant, and every Teams client rendering variant. The observed Teams client rendered the Bot Framework OAuth flow as a sign-in link fallback; the fallback and six-digit completion path were tested.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before consent, `msteams_whoami` returned `Microsoft Teams delegated auth unavailable: missing_consent`.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: N/A. This PR adds a new capability.
- Missing detection / guardrail: N/A.
- Contributing context (if known): Existing plugin tool execution had no channel-delegated auth context or Teams SSO consent bridge.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

N/A for a new feature, but the smallest reliable guardrails added/used are:

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test

- Scenario the test should lock in: Delegated auth is available only when policy allows it, propagates through agent/tool execution paths, survives cached plugin descriptors, handles Teams missing-consent/sign-in flows, and does not swallow ordinary six-digit messages without a pending auth challenge.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: These tests cover the generic plugin policy seam, the Teams SSO edge cases, and the runtime paths that carry hidden delegated-auth context without requiring live Microsoft infrastructure in CI.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): N/A before this PR.
- If no new test is added, why not: New tests were added/updated.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Plugin authors can opt into delegated auth with `plugins.entries.<pluginId>.auth.delegatedAccess`.
- Microsoft Teams plugin tools can request a Teams delegated token for the current user/conversation when explicitly allowlisted by config.
- Teams users may see a Bot Framework sign-in link/fallback when a delegated-auth tool needs consent.
- Added docs for Teams delegated-auth setup and plugin author usage.
- Added `examples/plugins/msteams-graph-profile` and `examples/msteams-obo-downstream-api`.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
Teams message -> agent -> plugin tool -> no delegated Teams user token -> downstream OBO unavailable

After:
Teams message -> Teams SSO provider -> gated plugin ctx.auth -> plugin tool -> downstream API OBO -> Microsoft Graph profile
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes`)
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes`)
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: Delegated Teams tokens are sensitive. This PR keeps access opt-in and policy-gated by plugin/tool allowlists plus provider, audience, scope, user, tenant, chat, and chat-type checks. Tokens are passed as hidden runtime context to plugin execution, not prompt text or transcript content. The example keeps Microsoft Graph access server-side in a downstream API so client secrets and Graph permissions stay behind an API boundary.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node/pnpm local dev checkout
- Model/provider: OpenAI dev agent profile
- Integration/channel (if any): Microsoft Teams dev app via devtunnel, Bot Framework OAuth connection
- Relevant config (redacted): Teams channel enabled, delegated-auth plugin entry enabled, local downstream OBO API configured with redacted client secret and app ids.

### Steps

1. Start devtunnel for the Teams bot endpoint on port 3978.
2. Start the local downstream OBO API.
3. Start `pnpm openclaw --dev gateway`.
4. Send `hi, run teams whoami` in Teams.
5. Complete the Bot Framework sign-in link and send the six-digit fallback code.
6. Retry `hi, run teams whoami`.

### Expected

- First run requests consent.
- Six-digit fallback completes delegated auth.
- Retried tool returns the signed-in Teams user profile/email.

### Actual

- First run returned `missing_consent`.
- Teams received the Bot Framework sign-in link.
- Six-digit fallback completed with `Microsoft Teams delegated auth is connected. Retry the tool now.`
- Retried `msteams_whoami` returned the signed-in Teams user profile/email.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: Teams missing-consent flow, Bot Framework sign-in link fallback, six-digit code completion, retrying `msteams_whoami`, and downstream OBO profile lookup.
- Edge cases checked: Six-digit messages are handled only while a pending sign-in challenge exists; delegated auth is rejected when missing/unconfigured/unavailable; Teams user-id fallback paths are covered by tests.
- What you did **not** verify: Non-Teams channels, production tenant rollout, hosted downstream API deployment, and every Teams client native OAuth-card rendering variant.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`Yes`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: Existing configs continue to work. To use delegated auth, explicitly configure `plugins.entries.<pluginId>.auth.delegatedAccess` and the Teams Bot Framework OAuth connection described in the docs.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: A plugin could receive a user token unexpectedly.
  - Mitigation: Delegated auth is opt-in, allowlist-gated, and claim-validated before tool execution.
- Risk: Teams clients may render OAuth consent as a sign-in link instead of a native card.
  - Mitigation: The Teams implementation supports sign-in-link fallback and six-digit completion.
- Risk: Downstream API consent is separate from Teams bot consent.
  - Mitigation: Docs and examples use separate app registrations and document admin pre-consent for the downstream API.

## Rationale And Design Decisions

### Keep core generic

Delegated auth is modeled as a generic plugin capability instead of a Teams-specific special case in core. Core owns policy parsing, tool gating, token claim validation, and runtime propagation; the Teams plugin owns Bot Framework SSO behavior and token acquisition.

### Make delegated auth explicit and policy-gated

Plugin delegated auth is opt-in through `plugins.entries.<pluginId>.auth.delegatedAccess.enabled`, with optional provider, audience, scope, user, tenant, chat, and chat-type restrictions.

### Keep optional tools least-privilege

Optional plugin factories receive `ctx.auth` only when the plugin itself, `group:plugins`, `*`, or a concrete optional tool name is allowlisted. The resolver also handles implicit optional registrations where `names: []` and `declaredNames` carry the actual tool contract.

### Resolve auth per execution for cached descriptors

Cached plugin tool descriptors keep descriptor creation fast, but delegated auth is resolved when the cached tool executes, so a previous message’s auth context is never cached into a future run.

### Propagate auth through run plumbing, not prompts

The Teams delegated auth context is passed through hidden runtime/run parameters and plugin tool context, including queued replies, follow-up runs, embedded runner attempts, OpenClaw tools, and Codex app-server tool calls.

### Teams owns Bot Framework SSO details

The Teams plugin owns Bot Framework token exchange, verify-state, sign-in resource creation, sign-in-link fallback, six-digit code fallback, and Teams user-id fallback handling.

### Keep Graph access server-side in the example

The example plugin calls a local downstream API. The downstream API performs Microsoft Graph OBO using its own app registration and delegated permission grant, which keeps Graph client secrets and broader Graph behavior behind a production-shaped API boundary.

target.title: fix #99712: surface empty interactive replies
target.body:
Fixes #99712.

## What Problem This Solves

Interactive direct reply/follow-up turns could finish with `runResult.payloads = []` and no committed source delivery, then silently return without telling the user anything.

## Why

For an interactive user turn, an empty final result is not a successful reply unless the run was explicitly allowed to be silent or already committed delivery through a source/message-tool path. The previous terminal checks existed in multiple places and left the auto-reply/follow-up boundary able to drop the reply.

## What Changed

- Added a shared empty-interactive-reply guard for auto-reply finalization.
- `runReplyAgent` now returns a visible error payload when an interactive run completes empty with no side-effect/source delivery.
- `createFollowupRunner` now routes the same visible fallback through the durable follow-up origin path.
- Preserved intentional silent cases:
  - heartbeat/silent expected turns
  - `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent`
  - `message_tool_only`
  - committed messaging/source-reply delivery
  - compaction notices and retrying compaction progress

## User Impact

Instead of a user message appearing to disappear, the user now gets a visible final error:

> I finished the turn, but it did not produce a visible reply. Please try again, or start a new session if this keeps happening.

## Evidence

Focused acceptance tests:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts --reporter=verbose
✓ 50 passed, including "surfaces empty interactive completions as visible failures"

  - "routes a visible fallback when an interactive followup completes empty"

  - compaction notice/retry regressions
```

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has many slash commands, but the iOS chat composer did not provide an in-context way to discover, filter, and select them. Users had to know command names ahead of time, and the composer did not have enough local slash-command awareness to present the Gateway command catalog cleanly.

This PR adds a slash command picker that opens when the user types `/`, shows a unified command/skill list, filters results as the user types, and inserts the selected command into the composer. It also wires the iOS Gateway command catalog transport through the active agent/session context so the picker reflects the correct command surface.

## Why This Change Was Made

The composer is the right place for command discovery because it keeps the user in message context while they choose a command. The current UI intentionally preserves monospace command names for scanability, but routes the text through `OpenClawChatTypography.mono(...)` so it follows the iOS branded typography policy.

## User Impact

Users can type `/` in chat and pick a command without memorizing command names. The picker now avoids category tabs/badges, keeps command rows compact, and includes a bottom scroll affordance when more commands are available.

## Evidence

target.title: refactor(security): consolidate secret primitives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Secret display masking and constant-time secret comparison were split across generic utilities, plugin-local wrappers, and ad hoc forwarding helpers. That duplicated security-sensitive contracts and made exact behavior harder to audit.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Move API-key and prefix-only secret display policies into the security owner boundary while preserving their distinct empty, short-value, control-character, prefix/suffix, and UTF-16 code-unit behavior.
- Keep constant-time string comparison as exact padded UTF-8 byte equality, including unconditional equal-length `timingSafeEqual` input and explicit original-length rejection.
- Remove Browser, Voice Call, Webhooks, and Zalo forwarding wrappers so callers use the canonical comparison directly.
- Add a narrow `openclaw/plugin-sdk/secret-display-runtime` entrypoint for Talk Voice instead of expanding the deprecated broad security barrel.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Existing masked output remains byte-for-byte stable for covered inputs, and authentication/webhook comparisons retain exact string equality without unequal-length short-circuiting.

target.title: ACP: add gateway-owned node-backed runtime
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: OpenClaw did not yet have a complete **node-backed ACP runtime** where the gateway owns the durable state and a paired node acts only as the execution worker.
- Why it matters: without that split, restart/replay/reconnect behavior is too dependent on the live process, which makes lease fencing, terminal resolution, and outward delivery recovery harder to reason about and prove.
- What this PR adds:
  - a durable ACP gateway store for sessions, runs, accepted worker events, leases, terminal state, replay targets, and projector checkpoints
  - gateway ingestion of ACP worker events coming back from paired nodes
  - a real node-host ACP worker bridge and gateway/node command plumbing
  - a durable ACP reply projection/replay path so restart recovery can resume from gateway state instead of only from the live iterator
  - startup recovery for incomplete ACP node runs
  - restart/reconnect/cancel/close race hardening with focused restart/replay test coverage
  - architecture / protocol / verification docs for the new backend
- Landing-only follow-up: after rebasing onto current `main`, this PR also includes a few **test-only** isolation fixes in Feishu / Google / Google Chat extension tests that were needed to make the landing branch green. Those are not ACP runtime behavior changes.

## What changed by area

### 1) Durable ACP gateway state

New ACP store/state plumbing under `src/acp/store/**`:

- persists ACP sessions and runs
- persists accepted worker events
- tracks leases / lease epochs
- resolves canonical terminal state on the gateway
- stores replay targets and projector checkpoints separately from the runtime cursor

This is the foundation that lets the gateway stay authoritative even when execution happens on a paired node.

### 2) Gateway ↔ node ACP worker path

Main implementation areas:

- `src/gateway/**`
- `src/infra/node-commands.ts`
- `src/node-host/**`

This adds the node-backed ACP execution path:

- gateway can start/control ACP work on a paired node
- node-host can run the ACP worker role
- worker events stream back to the gateway over the existing node transport
- gateway remains the source of truth for run state and terminal resolution

### 3) Durable reply projection and replay

Main implementation areas:

- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-replay.ts`

This PR moves ACP outward delivery onto a durable replayable path:

- reply targets are persisted per run
- projector checkpoints are advanced only after successful delivery
- restart recovery can replay the unfinished suffix from durable state
- reconnect and duplicate accepted events do not re-deliver already completed outward effects

### 4) Startup recovery / reconnect handling

Main implementation areas:

- `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-node-events.ts`
- `src/acp/runtime/acp-node.ts`

This adds the gateway-side recovery flow needed to:

- resume incomplete projection after restart
- keep reconnect handling deterministic
- prevent stale-worker wins
- preserve canonical terminal behavior across restart/replay windows

### 5) Test harnesses and regression coverage

Main test additions/expansions:

- `src/acp/store/store.restart.test.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.replay.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-node-events.acp.test.ts`
- `src/node-host/invoke-acp.test.ts`
- `src/acp/test-harness/restart-harness.ts`

These cover the core failure windows this backend needs to survive:

- restart after accepted events but before replay checkpoint advancement
- restart after terminal persistence but before final outward convergence
- reconnect replay of already accepted events
- cancel / complete / close race handling
- restart recovery with a real memory cut instead of reusing in-process objects

### 6) Docs included in this PR

Main docs:

- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime-protocol.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime-verification.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-runtime-program.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-slice4-summary.md`
- `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-slice4-final-judge.md`

These are included because this was developed as a staged architecture / verification effort and the final accepted behavior is documented there.

## Explicit scope boundaries / v1 limitations

This PR does **not**:

- turn nodes into mini-gateways
- add automatic cross-node continuation for an in-flight run
- claim durable resumed tool-message edit support after restart

Current conservative post-restart tool-update behavior remains:

- `append_only_after_restart`

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [x] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related: ACP node runtime architecture / protocol / verification docs under `docs/experiments/plans/`
- Related: landing-only extension test isolation fixes after rebase onto current `main`

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- OpenClaw now has a first-class ACP node-backed runtime path where the gateway owns durable ACP truth and paired nodes execute the worker role.
- Gateway restart/recovery can resume incomplete ACP outward projection from durable state.
- Duplicate accepted worker-event replay on reconnect is hardened so it does not duplicate outward delivery.
- Post-restart tool updates intentionally follow the documented conservative v1 rule: `append_only_after_restart`.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? Yes
- Command/tool execution surface changed? Yes
- Data access scope changed? Yes

### Security / trust-boundary notes

- Paired nodes can now advertise ACP worker capability and receive ACP runtime commands over the existing gateway↔node trust boundary.
- Gateway↔node websocket traffic now carries ACP worker control / event flows in addition to existing node commands.
- Gateway now persists ACP runtime state needed for durable replay/recovery.
- The design mitigates stale-worker / duplicate-delivery risks via lease epochs, canonical terminal resolution, durable replay checkpoints, and reconnect/replay handling on the gateway.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux (landing worktree on vm1) + GitHub Actions CI
- Runtime/container: Node / pnpm; Bun build path also checked
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): ACP gateway↔node runtime path
- Relevant config (redacted): ACP runtime restart/replay harnesses and paired-node fixtures

### Verified locally

- ACP targeted verification gate:
  - `pnpm test -- src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.replay.test.ts src/acp/store/store.test.ts src/acp/store/store.restart.test.ts src/acp/store/gateway-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-node-events.acp.test.ts src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-acp.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.acp.test.ts`
- TypeScript guardrail:
  - `pnpm tsgo`
- Landing-only extension test fixes:
  - `pnpm test:extensions`

### CI / build notes

- `pnpm build` still fails only with the pre-existing Bun wrapper issue:
  - `Cannot find module './cjs/index.cjs' from ''`
- That build failure was already present and is not introduced by the ACP runtime changes in this PR.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What I personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified the ACP-focused local gate listed above.
- Verified `pnpm tsgo` passes.
- Verified the rebased landing branch’s extension test-isolation fixes with local `pnpm test:extensions`.
- Verified the PR now includes the architecture / protocol / verification / final-judge docs for this backend.

What I did **not** verify:

- I did **not** get a clean `pnpm build` because of the pre-existing Bun wrapper failure noted above.
- I did **not** run a fresh manual end-to-end Discord/real-node interactive repro outside the checked-in restart/replay and node-host harnesses.

## Review Guide

If you want the shortest path through this PR, review in this order:

1. **Core architecture / intent**
   - `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime.md`
   - `docs/experiments/plans/acp-node-backed-runtime-protocol.md`
2. **Gateway-owned durable state**
   - `src/acp/store/**`
3. **Node execution bridge**
   - `src/node-host/**`
   - `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts`
   - `src/gateway/server-node-events.ts`
4. **Durable outward replay path**
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts`
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-replay.ts`
5. **Recovery and proofs**
   - `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.ts`
   - `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.replay.test.ts`
   - `src/gateway/server-startup.acp-node.test.ts`
6. **Ignore as landing-only test fixes unless you are checking CI fallout**
   - `extensions/feishu/**`
   - `extensions/google/**`
   - `extensions/googlechat/**`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No explicit migration required
- Migration needed? No

Notes:

- This adds a new ACP runtime/backend path; it does not force existing deployments to switch to it immediately.
- Post-restart tool updates intentionally remain append-only in v1.

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: revert this PR or avoid selecting/using the `acp-node` runtime path until fixed.
- Files/config to restore: ACP runtime/store/gateway/node-host changes under `src/acp/**`, `src/node-host/**`, `src/gateway/**`, plus the accompanying docs if reverting wholesale.
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: duplicate final delivery after restart, stale worker winning after reconnect, projector checkpoint drift, or replay targeting the wrong route.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: restart/replay correctness is subtle in any durable projection system.
  - Mitigation: this PR includes restart harnesses, startup recovery tests, reconnect/replay ordering tests, and explicit protocol/verification docs.
- Risk: the PR is large and spans multiple ACP runtime layers.
  - Mitigation: the review guide above splits it into durable store, node bridge, replay path, recovery path, and landing-only CI fixes.
- Risk: paired-node ACP execution expands the gateway↔node command surface.
  - Mitigation: the gateway remains authoritative for leases, terminal resolution, checkpoints, and replay instead of trusting node-local completion.

---

target.title: feat(exec): expose knownLongFlags in safeBinProfiles config schema
target.body:
## Summary

Expose the `knownLongFlags` field in the `safeBinProfiles` config schema, allowing operators to declare long flags as "known" for GNU abbreviation resolution without misusing `allowedValueFlags` or `deniedFlags`.

Closes #56805

> **Rebased 2026-06-10.** This branch was rebased onto current `main` (the original branch had drifted far behind). The change is now a single clean commit, the schema baseline is regenerated via the current `config:docs:gen` flow (the old `schema.base.generated.ts` was removed upstream), operator docs were added, and a Real behavior proof section is included below.

## Problem

The `knownLongFlags` field exists internally in `SafeBinProfile` and is used by `validateSafeBinArgv` for GNU long-option abbreviation resolution. However, it is not present in:

1. The Zod schema (`ToolExecSafeBinProfileSchema`) — `.strict()` rejects it as an unknown key
2. The `SafeBinProfileFixture` type — no way to pass it through config normalization

For empty profiles `{}`, `knownLongFlags` auto-derives as `[]`, causing **all** long flags to be treated as unknown and rejected. The only workaround is to list every possible long flag in `allowedValueFlags` or `deniedFlags`, which changes their semantics.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags: z.array(z.string()).optional()` to `ToolExecSafeBinProfileSchema` |
| `src/infra/exec-safe-bin-policy-profiles.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags` to `SafeBinProfileFixture`; normalize it in `normalizeSafeBinProfileFixture`; merge user-provided with auto-derived flags in `compileSafeBinProfile`, filtering strict prefixes of denied flags |
| `src/config/normalize-exec-safe-bin.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags` to the type cast in normalization |
| `docs/tools/exec-approvals-advanced.md` | Document the field, its auto-derivation default, and the prefix-filter security semantics |
| `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` | Regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen` for the new field |
| `src/infra/exec-safe-bin-policy.test.ts` | 8 new tests for the config path + security filter |

## Design Decisions

- **Merge, don't replace**: User-provided `knownLongFlags` are merged with auto-derived flags from `allowedValueFlags ∪ deniedFlags`, so flags in those lists stay "known" even if not explicitly listed.
- **Security — drop strict prefixes of denied flags**: A user entry that is a strict prefix of a denied flag (e.g. `--rec` when `--recursive` is denied) is filtered at compile time, so it cannot gain exact-match priority in `resolveCanonicalLongFlag` and bypass the denial. (Addresses the prior Codex review P1.)
- **Reuses `normalizeFixtureFlags`**: Same normalization (trim, dedupe, sort) as other flag arrays.
- **Backwards-compatible**: Existing configs without `knownLongFlags` work identically via auto-derivation.

## Usage

```json5
{
  tools: {
    exec: {
      safeBins: ["mycli"],
      safeBinProfiles: {
        mycli: {
          allowedValueFlags: ["--limit"],
          deniedFlags: ["--recursive"],
          knownLongFlags: ["--dry-run", "--verbose"],
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Setting `tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.<bin>.knownLongFlags` in a real config previously could not be accepted — the strict Zod schema had no such key. After this patch the field is accepted by config validation and is honored by the safe-bin argv validator (declared long flags resolve, including GNU abbreviation), while strict prefixes of denied flags are still blocked.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw build from this branch, `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (bb6e477)`, Node v22.22.0, run via the real `openclaw` CLI and the compiled `exec-safe-bin-policy` module (not mocks).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
# 1) Real CLI accepts a config containing knownLongFlags
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/klf-proof.json5 openclaw config validate --json
# config: { tools: { exec: { safeBins: ["mycli"], safeBinProfiles: {
#   mycli: { allowedValueFlags: ["--limit"], deniedFlags: ["--recursive"],
#            knownLongFlags: ["--dry-run", "--verbose"] } } } } }

# 2) Same CLI still rejects an unknown key (the pre-fix state of knownLongFlags)
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/klf-proof-unknown.json5 openclaw config validate --json
#   ( mycli: { knownLongFlagsTYPO: ["--dry-run"] } )

# 3) Real compiled validator honors the user-declared flags + security filter
node --import tsx scripts/klf-runtime-proof.mts
```

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
# step 1 — openclaw config validate (knownLongFlags present)
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/klf-proof.json5"}

# step 2 — openclaw config validate (unknown key knownLongFlagsTYPO)
{"valid":false,"path":"/tmp/klf-proof-unknown.json5",
 "issues":[{"path":"tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.mycli","message":"Invalid input"}]}

# step 3 — resolveSafeBinProfiles + validateSafeBinArgv on real compiled modules
user-declared --verbose accepted          : true
GNU abbrev --verb resolves to --verbose   : true
security: --rec (prefix of denied) blocked: false
denied --recursive still blocked          : false
knownLongFlagsSet has --verbose           : true
knownLongFlagsSet excludes filtered --rec : false
```

**Observed result after fix:** The live `openclaw config validate` returns `valid: true` for a config carrying `knownLongFlags`, and still returns `valid: false` for an unknown sibling key — confirming the field is genuinely wired into the strict schema. target.title: fix(gateway): defer hot-reload restart when dist/entry.js is missing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pushing commits into a live production git checkout triggers the gateway's hot-reload while `dist/` is mid-rebuild. The watcher (`requestRestart()` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`) immediately sends SIGTERM to the current healthy child process without checking whether the replacement build is valid for the new checkout state. The new child cannot start → crash-loop until systemd's start-limit is exhausted (37-min outage, P1, issue #99603).

## Changes

Two guard points using `isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs, resolveHead)` in `scripts/watch-node.mjs`:

### Guard 1 — requestRestart()

Before sending SIGTERM, verify:
1. `dist/entry.js` exists
2. `dist/.buildstamp` git HEAD matches current checkout HEAD

If either check fails (mid-rebuild or stale build), skip the kill and log. The running process is already loaded in memory and continues serving traffic. Restart will trigger on the next relevant file change.

### Guard 2 — Exit handler

When a child exits with SIGTERM/143, verify build readiness before restarting. If the build is not ready (rebuild was interrupted), settle the watcher so systemd restarts the process tree cleanly rather than crash-looping.

### Scope

Partial mitigation — prevents the crash-loop but keeps the existing stop-then-start restart ordering. Issue #99603 should remain open for a transactional restart (build-then-swap). Competing PR #99610 targets the same root cause; maintainers should choose one canonical repair.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Command: `npx tsx proof/hot-reload-race-guard.proof.ts`

```
HOT-RELOAD RACE GUARD PROOF
 Hostname: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
 PID:      <pid>
 Timestamp: 2026-07-03 18:49:10

 ─── 1. Production code: isBuildReadyForRestart ───
   ✅ Imported from scripts/watch-node.mjs

 ─── 2. Pure function: entry.js + build stamp checks ───
   ✅ entry.js missing → false
   ✅ entry exists, no readFileSync → true (fallback)
   ✅ build stamp HEAD != git HEAD → false
   ✅ build stamp HEAD == git HEAD → true

 ─── 3. Real filesystem lifecycle ───
   ✅ empty dist/ → false
   ✅ entry.js exists, no stamp → false
   ✅ stamp HEAD matches git HEAD → true
   ✅ stamp HEAD != git HEAD → false (git push)
   ✅ re-synced stamp → true (rebuild complete)

 ─── 4. Source code verification ───
   ✅ requestRestart() uses isBuildReadyForRestart
   ✅ Exit handler uses isBuildReadyForRestart
   ✅ isBuildReadyForRestart is exported
   ✅ no polling (narrow fix)

 ─── 5-7. Tests + lint ───
   ✅ Tests 24 passed (including guard tests)
   ✅ All run-node + watch-node tests pass (no regression)
   ✅ Lint: 0 warnings, 0 errors

 RESULTS: 16 passed, 0 failed
```

```
# no type errors in changed files
```

target.title: fix(exec): require approval for OpenClaw lifecycle commands
target.body:
﻿﻿﻿﻿Fixes #99518

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where exec commands through gateway or node hosts could let OpenClaw gateway/daemon lifecycle mutations pass through normal allowlist or auto-review paths when they should require explicit approval.

The affected workflow is OpenClaw self-management from exec surfaces: stopping, starting, restarting, running, deleting, or uninstalling the gateway/daemon through CLI, launchctl, systemctl, schtasks, process-kill, shell-wrapper, package-manager, Windows shim, `env -S`, `sudo`/`doas`, and dispatch-wrapper commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a focused lifecycle classifier to the exec approval policy and wires it into both gateway-host and node-host approval analysis. The guard forces explicit approval for OpenClaw lifecycle mutations unless exec is already in yolo mode (`security=full`, `ask=off`).

The follow-up update also covers foreground gateway runtime forms that were missed by the first patch: `openclaw gateway`, `openclaw gateway run`, `openclaw gateway --force`, and option-only gateway run surfaces such as `--port`. Read-only gateway inspection remains outside the guard, including `openclaw gateway status`, `openclaw gateway call ...`, `openclaw gateway --help`, `openclaw gateway run --help`, `launchctl print`, `systemctl status`, `schtasks /Query`, and generic read-only process lookups.

## User Impact

Operators get an extra human confirmation before an agent or auto-review path can stop, start, restart, run, delete, or uninstall the OpenClaw gateway/daemon in non-yolo configurations. Existing yolo-mode behavior and read-only status/query commands are unchanged.

## Evidence

Issue review feedback incorporated: lifecycle classification now has regression coverage for the ordering invariant that classification happens before durable allowlist trust or auto-review decisions.

Latest review feedback incorporated at `d6c702f501c6`: systemctl action discovery now skips value-taking options before the lifecycle verb, so `systemctl -s TERM kill openclaw-gateway.service` and `systemctl --signal=TERM kill openclaw-gateway.service` are classified before allowlist or auto-review can run. A read-only regression keeps `systemctl --type service status openclaw-gateway.service` outside the lifecycle guard.

Live gateway-host proof from an isolated branch gateway (`node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port <random> --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured`, independent temp state/config):

```json
{
  "branchHead": "0ce214f5c1a1",
  "isolatedGateway": {
    "healthOk": true
  },

    "command": "openclaw gateway --force",
    "autoReviewCalls": 0,

    "warningCount": 1

  "yoloFullOff": {
    "command": "openclaw gateway --force",
    "allowedWithoutPending": true,
    "warningCount": 0
  }
}
```

`approval-unavailable` is expected in this isolated proof because no approval delivery route is configured; it is still a blocking approval result before command execution, and `autoReviewCalls: 0` proves the lifecycle command was not laundered through auto-review first. The `yoloFullOff` case confirms `security=full` + `ask=off` remains unchanged.

- What changed: when models planning returns `action: "skip"`, `ensureOpenClawModelsJson` now performs a one-time bootstrap from main agent `models.json` only if target is non-main and target `models.json` is missing.

target.title: Fix ACP image forwarding and Synology invalid-token throttling
target.body:
## Summary

This PR bundles two small, low-risk fixes:

1. Fix ACP attachment collection so URL-only image attachments are forwarded into ACP turns.
2. Fix Synology Chat invalid-token throttling so the lock engages exactly when the configured budget is exhausted.

## What changed

### ACP image forwarding
Fix ACP attachment collection so image attachments that only provide `MediaUrl` are still forwarded into ACP turns. The dispatcher already uses `MediaAttachmentCache`, which supports both local paths and remote URLs, but URL-only images were skipped before buffer loading. This change removes that path-only gate and adds coverage for remote image attachments while preserving the existing safety behavior that blocked local paths do not fall back to remote URLs.

### Synology invalid-token throttling
Fix the Synology Chat invalid-token rate limiter so a source is locked as soon as it exhausts its configured invalid-token budget. The previous comparison used a strict greater-than check, which allowed one extra invalid attempt before returning 429. target.title: feat(irc): support markdown messages via draft/multiline
target.body:
## Summary

Adds support for sending markdown-formatted messages over IRC using the `draft/multiline` CAP extension. This preserves newlines in bot responses, allowing IRC clients to properly render markdown content.

## Motivation

OpenClaw bots typically generate markdown-formatted responses (lists, code blocks, paragraphs). Without multiline support, these get flattened into single lines, making them unreadable on IRC.

The `draft/multiline` spec (https://ircv3.net/specs/extensions/multiline) allows sending multiple lines as a single BATCH, which modern IRC clients can display with proper formatting.

## Changes

- **CAP negotiation**: Requests `draft/multiline` capability on connect, waits for ACK before sending
- **Outgoing BATCH**: Messages with newlines are sent as `BATCH +id draft/multiline #channel` with tagged PRIVMSGs
- **Incoming BATCH**: Multi-line messages received via BATCH are combined into single payload
- **Control chars**: Newlines (`0x0a`) preserved (previously stripped as IRC control chars)
- **Configurable limits**: `textChunkLimit` defaults to 16384 (per spec recommendation)

## Compatibility

- **Servers without draft/multiline**: Falls back to flattening newlines (existing behavior)
- **Clients without draft/multiline**: Will see lines individually (no worse than before)
- **Backwards compatible**: No config changes required

## Testing

Tested on Ergo IRC server with `draft/multiline` support. Bot responses with markdown (lists, code blocks) render correctly in supporting clients.

target.title: refactor(qa): unify live channel runtime hosting
target.body:
Closes #99699

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, and Matrix live QA commands each owned a separate runtime invocation path. Matrix also lived in its own QA runner plugin, so QA Lab could not host it through the same composable adapter registry without importing plugin-private implementation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The four existing live runtimes now contribute canonical asynchronous `QaTransportAdapterFactory` implementations. QA Lab resolves them through its existing transport registry and runs their code-backed suites through the shared suite host; Matrix contributes its factory beside its CLI registration through the owner-neutral QA runner runtime surface, so neither plugin imports the other's private modules.

The shipped registration-only QA runner contract remains a narrow compatibility mount path. It is documented by `qaRunners` plus `qaRunnerCliRegistrations` and was released through the exported `openclaw/plugin-sdk/qa-runner-runtime` subpath. Registration-only runners continue mounting their own command directly, but cannot enter the shared suite host without a factory. Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, and Matrix all use factories.

Matrix's deterministic forced-exit behavior remains at the Matrix-owned CLI boundary. Discord is unchanged. Crabline remains on published 0.1.9 and continues using its existing in-process event observer; this change does not restore recorder polling or add a capability manifest.

## User Impact

No production channel behavior changes. QA maintainers get one adapter registry and suite-host path for the four existing live channel commands, while channel-specific credentials, scenarios, artifacts, cleanup, and plugin ownership remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto `bc802ceee189376df32049056553ff422a678293` before final validation.
- Focused proof via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` covers QA runner discovery, registration-only compatibility, registry selection, Telegram/Slack/WhatsApp adapters, shared suite lifecycle, CLI routing, Matrix factory ownership, and Matrix forced exit: 100+ tests passed across the relevant Vitest shards.

target.title: fix(agents): hint when unknown tools are skills
target.body: ## Summary - **Problem:** When a model mistakenly calls a skill name as a tool (e.g. `my-skill`), the error message is a generic "Tool not found" with no guidance, so the model keeps retrying or gives up. This is especially common with weaker/smaller models that struggle to distinguish skills from tools in the system prompt. - **Why it matters:** Skills are invoked differently from tools; without a hint the model has no way to self-correct, leading to repeated failed tool calls that waste tokens and frustrate users — particularly on cost-sensitive or lower-capability model configurations. - **What changed:** Register an `afterToolCall` hook in `attempt.ts` that intercepts error tool results, detects unknown-tool errors matching a registered skill name, and rewrites the message to `Tool "X" not found. "X" is a skill. Read its SKILL.md first.` Also extracted `resolveUnknownToolName` helper in `errors.ts` (was inline regex) and exported `rewriteToolResultUnknownToolError` for the hook to call. - **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** `formatAssistantErrorText` signature and all its callers are untouched. No new params threaded through `run.ts`, `payloads.ts`, `subscribe.types.ts`, or lifecycle handlers. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Feature - [x] Refactor ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Skills / tool execution ## Linked Issue/PR None ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - When a model calls a skill name as a tool and the skill is registered, the error tool result now says: `Tool "X" not found. "X" is a skill. Read its SKILL.md first.` - When the tool name does not match any registered skill, behavior is unchanged (generic "Tool not found"). ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? `No` - Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No` - New/changed network calls? `No` - Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` - Data access scope changed? `No` ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS (Darwin 25.3.0, arm64) - Runtime/container: Node 22 + pnpm - Model/provider: Claude (Anthropic) - Relevant config: workspace with registered skills (e.g. `my-skill`, `another-skill`) ### Steps 1. Start an OpenClaw agent session with skills registered 2. Prompt the model to call a skill name as if it were a tool (e.g. "use tool my-skill") 3. Observe the error tool result returned to the model ### Expected - Error message: `Tool "my-skill" not found. "my-skill" is a skill. target.title: fix(security): use constant-time comparison for TLS fingerprint verification
target.body:
## Summary

TLS certificate fingerprint verification in `src/gateway/client.ts` uses `!==` (standard JavaScript string equality), which is vulnerable to **timing side-channel attacks** (CWE-208).

An attacker on the network path can measure response time differences to iteratively guess the correct fingerprint byte-by-byte, potentially bypassing TLS pinning for MITM attacks on gateway connections.

## Root cause

Two locations perform fingerprint comparison with `!==`:

| Location | Context |
|----------|---------|
| Line 205 | WebSocket `checkServerIdentity` callback |
| Line 681 | HTTP `validateTlsFingerprint` method |

## Fix

Replace both with `safeEqualSecret()` from `src/security/secret-equal.ts`, which uses `SHA-256` hashing + `crypto.timingSafeEqual` for constant-time comparison.

This is the **same function already used** for pairing token verification elsewhere in the codebase — just missed for TLS fingerprints.

```diff
- if (fingerprint !== expected) {
+ if (!safeEqualSecret(fingerprint, expected)) {
```

## Why safeEqualSecret and not raw timingSafeEqual

`timingSafeEqual` requires both buffers to have equal length, which would leak the length of the expected fingerprint. `safeEqualSecret` avoids this by hashing both values with SHA-256 first (producing fixed 32-byte digests), then comparing the digests in constant time.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm tsgo` — compiles cleanly
- [x] `pnpm check` — lint/format passes
- [x] Existing `safeEqualSecret` tests in `src/security/audit-extra.sync.test.ts` cover equal, unequal, different-length, and undefined inputs
- [x] No remaining `fingerprint !== expected` patterns in codebase

## Summary

This PR fixes an issue where heartbeat polls could overwrite explicit user-labeled session titles with transcript-derived titles like `"heartbeat"`.

## Changes

- Extracts `deriveSessionTitle` to `session-title.ts` with a dedicated test module.
- Preserves explicit session labels before transcript-derived fallbacks.
- Keeps auto-populated `origin.label` behind `firstUserMessage` so unlabeled inbound DMs can still use transcript-derived titles.
- Keeps `session-utils.ts` as a compatibility re-export site.
- Clarifies the zero timestamp test name to describe the actual `updatedAt: 0` input.

## Title precedence

1. `displayName`
2. `subject`
3. explicit `entry.label`
4. `firstUserMessage` (truncated)
5. auto-populated `entry.origin?.label`
6. `sessionId` prefix fallback

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: explicit session labels should survive heartbeat-style transcript summaries, while auto-populated origin labels should not override a real first user message.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout on this branch after rebasing onto current `main`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx --eval 'import { deriveSessionTitle } from "./src/gateway/session-title.ts";
const cases = {
  explicitLabelBeatsHeartbeat: deriveSessionTitle({ sessionId: "abc123", updatedAt: Date.now(), label: "My App - Dashboard" }, "heartbeat"),
  transcriptBeatsAutoOriginLabel: deriveSessionTitle({ sessionId: "abc123", updatedAt: Date.now(), origin: { label: "Discord: Engineering" } }, "Need help with deployment"),
  originLabelFallbackWithoutTranscript: deriveSessionTitle({ sessionId: "abc123", updatedAt: Date.now(), origin: { label: "Discord: Engineering" } }, null),
  zeroUpdatedAtFallback: deriveSessionTitle({ sessionId: "abcd1234-5678-90ef-ghij-klmnopqrstuv", updatedAt: 0 }),
};
console.log(JSON.stringify(cases, null, 2));'
```

Evidence after fix:

```json
  "transcriptBeatsAutoOriginLabel": "Need help with deployment",
  "originLabelFallbackWithoutTranscript": "Discord: Engineering",
  "zeroUpdatedAtFallback": "abcd1234"
```

target.title: fix: keep Codex delegation controls directly available
target.body:
Closes #99464
Related: #99561

AI-assisted. This branch preserves the original #99561 commits by @100yenadmin and adjusts the final behavior to the independently validated fix direction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server users could be told that deferred OpenClaw delegation tools were searchable, but an explicit `tool_search` for `sessions_spawn` did not make the OpenClaw tool callable. The model could then answer without spawning the requested child session.

It also avoids changing the registered `heartbeat_respond` schema between normal and heartbeat turns on a resumed Codex thread.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the small, stable OpenClaw control set (`agents_list`, `sessions_spawn`, and `sessions_yield`) directly available on every Codex app-server turn. Broad tools remain deferred behind `tool_search`, and `heartbeat_respond` remains deferred with a stable registration across normal and heartbeat turns.

This keeps delegation controls reliable without making the entire OpenClaw tool catalog direct, and preserves the Codex app-server requirement that a resumed thread retain the same registered dynamic-tool definitions.

## User Impact

Codex app-server agents can reliably list agents, spawn subagents, and yield without depending on connector-oriented `tool_search` resolution. Existing deferred-tool behavior remains in place for the broader catalog, and heartbeat turns no longer risk a thread schema mismatch.

## Evidence

- Live AWS Crabbox before/after proof: run `run_0a496ddc9d30`, provider `aws`, lease `cbx_60d63e7d43b5` (`harbor-prawn`).

target.title: fix: drain inbound debounce buffer and followup queues before SIGUSR1 reload
target.body:
## Problem

When `config.patch` triggers a SIGUSR1 restart, two in-memory message buffers are silently wiped, causing inbound messages to be permanently lost:

1. **Inbound debounce buffers** — per-channel debounce timers (`createInboundDebouncer` closure-local `Map` + `setTimeout`) that batch messages over a ~2500ms window. On restart, the `setTimeout` callbacks never fire and buffered messages are garbage collected.

2. **Followup queues** — the `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES` global `Map` that collects messages for sessions with active agent turns. Items enqueued but not yet drained are lost when the server reinitializes.

### Reproduction
Send a message on Signal → within 2.5s, trigger a config change (e.g. `config.patch`) → the message is silently dropped.

## Fix

### 1. Global debouncer registry (`src/auto-reply/inbound-debounce.ts`)
- Each `createInboundDebouncer()` now auto-registers in a shared `Symbol.for('openclaw.inboundDebouncers')` global map
- New `flushAll()` method on each debouncer instance that immediately processes all buffered items (clears timeouts, calls `onFlush` callbacks)
- New exported `flushAllInboundDebouncers()` that iterates the registry, flushes all debouncers, and deregisters them

### 2. Followup queue drain waiter (`src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain-all.ts`)
- New `waitForFollowupQueueDrain(timeoutMs)` that polls `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES` until all queues finish processing (or timeout)
- Counts `draining: true` queues as having pending work even if `items.length` is momentarily 0

### 3. SIGUSR1 restart integration (`src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts`)
Before `markGatewayDraining()`, the restart flow now:
1. `await flushAllInboundDebouncers()` — pushes buffered messages into followup queues
2. `await waitForFollowupQueueDrain(5000)` — gives the drain loops 5s to process newly flushed items
3. Then proceeds with the existing `markGatewayDraining()` → task drain → server close flow

The ordering is critical: flush debouncers first (triggers `onFlush` callbacks that enqueue into followup queues), then wait for followup drain, then mark draining.

## Tests

- **`src/auto-reply/inbound.test.ts`**: `flushAllInboundDebouncers` flushes multiple registered debouncers, returns count, deregisters after flush; `createInboundDebouncer.flushAll` flushes all buffered keys
- **`src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain-all.test.ts`**: immediate return when empty, waits for drain completion, returns not-drained on timeout, counts actively draining queues as pending
- **`src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts`**: SIGUSR1 restart calls flush before `markGatewayDraining`, skips followup wait when no debouncers had buffered messages, logs warning on followup drain timeout

All 118 tests pass across the 4 affected test files. No type errors introduced.

## Files Changed
- `src/auto-reply/inbound-debounce.ts` — global registry + `flushAll` + `flushAllInboundDebouncers()`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain-all.ts` — new `waitForFollowupQueueDrain()`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/queue.ts` — barrel export
- `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts` — hook into restart flow
- Test files for all of the above

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: When a SIGUSR1 restart fires within the inbound debounce window (~2.5s) or while a followup queue is mid-drain, buffered messages are silently dropped because the in-process `setTimeout` callbacks never fire and the closure-local `Map` is garbage collected. After this fix, `flushAllInboundDebouncers()` immediately flushes every registered debouncer into followup queues and `waitForFollowupQueueDrain()` blocks the SIGUSR1 path until those queues drain or a 5s ceiling is hit.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at HEAD `5d1e6592d02782361b871581c10a6b3c0329105f` of branch `fix/drain-queue-before-sigusr1`. Linux 6.12.67, Node v24.15.0, pnpm-driven monorepo. Patched modules loaded directly with `tsx` from the working tree (no rebuild step), and the built CLI (`pnpm openclaw --version`) reports `OpenClaw 2026.5.4 (5d1e659)` confirming the binary is built from the patched commit.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. `pnpm openclaw --version` to confirm the live CLI is built from the patched HEAD.
